The challenge

Green hydrogen deployment is limited

Until now, cost and scalability have limited the adoption of green hydrogen. Three things are holding back conventional electrolysers.

EFFICIENCY

Moderate efficiency

Bubbles and resistive losses cap conventional stacks at roughly 70 to 80% efficiency, leading to large electricity costs.

MATERIALS

Critical materials

PEM electrolysers depend on scarce iridium and Nafion membranes, tying cost and scale-up to fragile supply chains.

FLEXIBILITY

Inflexible operation

Low power density and limited load cycling hold alkaline systems back when paired with fluctuating renewable power.

Our proposition

The Hollow Core Electrolyser

Pora's Hollow Core membrane-free electrolyser delivers a new way to generate hydrogen while overcoming the challenges facing standard green hydrogen electrolysers.

Lower capital costs

Fewer components and no membrane cut the cost of the stack and the balance of plant around it.

Increased efficiency

Removing bubbles from the cell removes the resistive losses that hold conventional stacks back.

Enhanced adaptability

Stable operation across a wide load range, matching the swings of wind and solar power.

Markets

Our target markets

Cheap electrolysis unlocks decarbonisation in industries where hydrogen is the feedstock.

NH₃

Green ammonia

Fertilizer production is one of the largest hydrogen consumers on Earth.

DRI

Green steel

Direct reduced iron with hydrogen replaces coal in steelmaking.

REFINING

Refining and chemicals

Refineries, methanol, and hydrogenation processes already run on hydrogen at massive scale, with e-fuels adding demand next.

Roadmap

From lab cell to industrial stack

2023 - 2026

Research foundations

Gas-breathing electrode concept developed in the Electrochemical Materials and Systems group at Eindhoven University of Technology. Laboratory pilot setup built and patent filed on the core invention.

2026

Validation with industry

Over 100 conversations with industrial hydrogen users, developers, and OEMs, alongside the construction of a first pilot system.

2027+

Spin-off and scale-up

Pora Technologies is founded as a TU/e spin-off and brings the Hollow Core Electrolyser to industrial scale.
